question: How do Marketplace alerts work? I saved a search but I'm not getting any matches.
answer:
A saved search is a standing watch: it only fires on listings posted AFTER you saved it. It never looks backwards, so an empty Matches list usually just means nothing new has been posted yet.

To create one: Alerts → "New search" (or "Save a search" if you have none), enter a Label (required — it names each match, e.g. "Cisco switch under $2k"), optionally set Keyword, Category, Max price and For sale / Wanted, then "Save search".

Why a search may never fire:
• Existing listings are never matched retroactively — only new posts.
• Every filter must match. Keyword is a plain substring of title, vendor or model. Category must be exactly the one the seller picked (a switch filed under "Other" won't match a Switches search).
• Kind must match: a "For sale" search never matches a Wanted post.
• Max price excludes anything above it; listings with no price ("Make an offer") still come through.
• You are never alerted about your own listings.

Limits: 20 saved searches max (the 21st gives "max 20 saved searches"); Alerts shows the 50 most recent. "Mark all read" clears the badge, the × on a row dismisses one match, and deleting a search ("Stop alerts and delete?") also removes its matches.
rootCause: matchAlerts() runs only inside the POST /api/marketplace/listings response wrapper, so it evaluates saved searches against newly inserted rows only; it skips the listing's own owner, requires kind and (if set) category equality, a substring hit on title+vendor+model, and max_price_cents >= price. Saved searches are capped at 20 per user; GET /alerts is LIMIT 50; alerts cascade-delete with their saved search.

evidence.snippet:
WHERE a.user_id = ?
    ORDER BY a.created_at DESC LIMIT 50
How this search is named in your alerts.

question: My listing disappeared from Browse and now shows "closed" — I didn't touch it.
answer:
Listings auto-retire at 90 days. Any listing still "active" 90 days after it was posted is flipped to "closed" — it drops out of Browse (Browse only shows active listings) but stays in My listings with a grey "closed" pill.

To bring it back:
1. Open My listings (closed listings are still there — they only vanish from public Browse).
2. Press "Relist" — it goes straight back to active and reappears in Browse.
3. If the gear is gone, press Delete, then "Yes, delete".

Other reasons a listing leaves Browse:
• It shows "sold" — you pressed "Mark sold", or a buyer took the last unit, which marks it sold automatically.
• Your platform owner hid it after it was reported. That also shows as "closed"; relisting without fixing the problem just gets it hidden again, so ask them what was wrong first.

Note: the expiry sweep is lazy (it runs at most once an hour, and only when certain pages are loaded), so a listing may sit past 90 days for a while before it flips.

The Dashboard's "Closed" tile ("Expired or withdrawn") counts both cases.
rootCause: maybeExpireListings() flips any active listing created more than 90 days ago to 'closed'. It is debounced to once an hour and is registered as router.use AFTER most /api/marketplace routes, so in practice it only fires on the later-registered endpoints (dashboard, stripe/status, partner OAuth status) rather than on every request.

evidence.snippet: <Stat label="Closed"   value={d.listings.closed} meta="Expired or withdrawn" />

question: What do the numbers on the Marketplace Dashboard mean, and why is my revenue zero when I've sold things?
answer:
The Marketplace Dashboard ("Seller dashboard — Listings, sales and purchases") is per-user, not per-organization, and Revenue counts completed orders only.

What the numbers are:
• Listings — Total, Active, Sold, Closed ("Expired or withdrawn").
• Sales — Revenue ("From N completed orders"), Orders (all orders where you're the seller), Completed, and Pending ("Awaiting shipment"). Pending counts orders at Paid or Shipped — it's your to-ship / to-close queue, not unpaid orders.
• Purchases — Spent ("Across N orders") and your buyer order count.

Why Revenue reads zero: only orders with status Completed are totalled. An order still at Paid or Shipped sits in Pending and contributes nothing. Close them out: Orders → Selling → open the order → "Mark completed" → "Yes, complete". The button only appears once the order is Shipped, so mark it shipped first.

There is no combined org view — if several admins in your org sell, each sees only their own figures. "Recent listings" shows your last ten; "View all" opens the My listings tab.
symptoms: Dashboard doesn't show my team's sales
rootCause: GET /api/marketplace/dashboard aggregates strictly by req.user.id: revenue_cents sums total_cents only WHERE status='completed', pending_orders counts status IN ('paid','shipped'), and there is no organization-level rollup.

evidence.snippet:
const orderStats = db.prepare(`
    SELECT
      COUNT(*)                                   AS total_orders,
      SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS completed_orders,
      SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'completed' THEN total_cents ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_cents,
      SUM(CASE WHEN status IN ('paid','shipped') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)   AS pending_orders
    FROM marketplace_orders WHERE seller_id = ?
  `).get(uid);

<StatGroup title="Sales">
            <Stat
              lead
              label="Revenue"
              value={formatCurrency(d.sales.revenueCents)}
              meta={`From ${plural(d.sales.completedOrders, 'completed order')}`}
            />
...
            <Stat
              label="Pending"

question: What do Partner accounts do, and how do I get new listings posted into our Discord channel?
answer:
Partners (/marketplace/partners, admin only) shows three cards — eBay, Amazon, Discord — each with a Connected / Not connected pill. Discord is the only one that does anything today.

Discord (announce new listings in a channel):
1. Discord: Channel settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy webhook URL.
2. RackTrack: Partners → Discord → paste into "Webhook URL" → "Save webhook".
3. Press "Send test". You should see "Test notification sent to Discord." here and a "Webhook Test" message in the channel.
4. After that, every listing anyone creates posts a card with title, category, condition, price, equipment and location. The fan-out is server-wide, not per-user: every connected Discord webhook gets it.

If the test fails:
• "No Discord webhook connected" — it was disconnected; save the URL again.
• "Webhook failed: Discord returned 404" — the webhook was deleted in Discord; create a new one and save it.

eBay / Amazon: if Connect is greyed out with "API keys not configured on this server", the server has no eBay/Amazon credentials — ask your platform owner. When they are configured, Connect starts an OAuth redirect, but neither platform cross-posts listings yet.

Disconnect → "Yes, disconnect" stops the webhook being used immediately.
symptoms: API keys not configured on this server
rootCause: POST /api/marketplace/partner-accounts stores one row per (user, platform); Discord requires a webhookUrl and is the only platform actually consumed — sendDiscordNotification() fans out to every connected discord webhook after a listing insert. eBay/Amazon Connect is disabled client-side when the corresponding /status endpoint reports configured:false.

question: INTERNAL: A buyer says they paid but the order is still Pending — how does Marketplace payment actually work?
answer:
Marketplace payment is env-gated and the order's initial status depends on whether Stripe is wired up: `const initialStatus = stripe ? 'pending' : 'paid'` (server/marketplace_routes.js:642).

Check GET /api/marketplace/stripe/status ({configured:true|false}) first.

configured:false — no charge is ever taken. POST /api/marketplace/orders writes the order straight in as 'paid' ("offline payment assumed"). The checkout button reads "Complete purchase — …". Treat it as an IOU settled outside RackTrack; never tell a customer RackTrack charged them.

configured:true — the order is written 'pending', a Checkout Session is created with the order id in metadata, and the client redirects to session.url (MarketplaceCheckoutPage.jsx:113-117). The only path to 'paid' is POST /api/marketplace/stripe/webhook receiving checkout.session.completed, matching metadata.orderId, and running an UPDATE guarded by `AND status = 'pending'` (marketplace_routes.js:1310-1330).

Known defect — the webhook currently cannot work. server/app.js:284 mounts express.json() globally before the marketplace router (app.js:434), so the route's express.raw() is skipped and req.body arrives as a parsed object. With STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET set, constructEvent throws; without it, JSON.parse on an object throws. Either way the response is 400 "Webhook verification failed: …". So on any deployment with Stripe enabled, orders never leave Pending. Fix is server-side: mount the webhook with express.raw before express.json.

Other ways an order sits at Pending: the buyer abandoned or failed the Stripe page (cancel_url returns them to /marketplace/orders/<id>?payment=cancelled, but MarketplaceOrdersPage never reads ?payment=, so they see no message and often assume it worked); or session creation itself failed, in which case the API returns { ok:true, order, stripeError } and the client — which only looks for stripeSessionUrl — silently drops them on a pending order page. Grep the log for marketplace.stripe_error.

There is no in-app way to re-drive payment on an existing order (only one create-session call site, at order creation). Cancel the order via PATCH /api/marketplace/orders/:id (allowed from pending) and have the buyer check out again.
symptoms: Buyer paid but status didn't change
No confirmation after returning from Stripe
rootCause: initialStatus = stripe ? 'pending' : 'paid'. Without Stripe the order is fabricated as paid with no charge; with Stripe the only path to 'paid' is the checkout.session.completed webhook, and both a cancelled session and a failed session-creation leave the order pending with no user-visible message because MarketplaceOrdersPage ignores ?payment=.

question: INTERNAL: An admin says "Connect eBay" (or Connect Amazon) just goes to a broken page even though the API keys are set.
answer:
Client bug, not credentials. Verify keys, then set expectations.

1. GET /api/marketplace/partner-accounts/ebay/status (or …/amazon/status). If `configured:false`, the Connect button is disabled with "API keys not configured on this server" — that IS the credentials case: set EBAY_APP_ID / EBAY_CERT_ID / EBAY_REDIRECT_URI (or AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_ID / AMAZON_SP_CLIENT_SECRET / AMAZON_REDIRECT_URI) in .env and restart.
2. If `configured:true`, the button works but the page is broken: …/auth-url returns `{ ok: true, url }` while the page reads `data.authUrl`, so it navigates to the literal string "undefined" — blank / not-found page, consent screen never reached (MarketplacePartnerAccountsPage.jsx:128 vs marketplace_routes.js:1349 and :1397).
3. No in-app workaround. POSTing /api/marketplace/partner-accounts with {platform:'ebay'} only creates a stub row — it grants no eBay access.
4. The callbacks redirect with ?error=ebay_auth_failed / ?error=amazon_auth_failed (and ?connected=ebay), but the page never reads query params, so a failed — or successful — exchange also shows nothing.

Even once connected, nothing cross-posts: no code publishes a RackTrack listing to eBay or Amazon. Never promise cross-posting.
symptoms: Connect eBay goes to a blank page
rootCause: MarketplacePartnerAccountsPage reads data.authUrl from the /auth-url response, but the server returns the field as `url`, so window.location.href is assigned undefined. Separately, the ?error=…/?connected=… params the OAuth callbacks redirect with are never read by the page.

evidence.snippet: return res.redirect(`${STRIPE_BASE_URL}/marketplace/partners?error=ebay_auth_failed`);

question: INTERNAL: A customer reported a listing and nothing happened. How does reporting and moderation work?
answer:
Reporting writes a row and stops there. Handle these tickets manually.

"Report listing" POSTs to /api/marketplace/listings/:id/flag, which only inserts into marketplace_flags (server/marketplace_routes.js:1139-1146). A repeat report from the same account hits the UNIQUE(listing_id,user_id) constraint and shows "already flagged" in the modal. The UI then says "Reported. An admin will review this listing." (client/src/pages/MarketplacePage.jsx:410-413) — that is not true; nobody is queued to see it.

Missing pieces:
- No endpoint or screen lists flags. marketplace_flags appears exactly twice in the codebase (CREATE TABLE + INSERT). The only way to read reports is querying server/data/auth.db directly.
- No notification fires on a flag. The Discord webhook is wired to listing creation only.
- POST /api/marketplace/listings/:id/moderate ('hide' → status closed, 'restore' → active) gates on `user.role === 'admin' || user.id === 1` (marketplace_routes.js:1156-1159). RackTrack never issues an 'admin' role — roles are owner, org_admin, site_manager, member (server/auth.js:211-214) — so only the first user row can moderate. Everyone else, platform owner included, gets 403 "admin only".

Resolution: escalate to whoever holds user id 1 on that deployment, or ask the seller to delete their own listing (DELETE /api/marketplace/listings/:id is owner-only and always works for them). Never promise the customer a review.
symptoms: Where do I review reported listings
Can't hide a listing as owner
rootCause: marketplace_flags is write-only — no list/read endpoint and no notification hook. The moderate endpoint gates on a role string ('admin') that the auth system never issues, falling back to user.id === 1, so owner/org_admin accounts receive 403 'admin only'.
